pairs.subject: markdown-vault
pairs.evidence: features/admin/getAdminData.ts:17 /admin reads docs/data-analysis (the vault: graph-log.md, frontier.md, batch-NNN.md) only for display, with tolerant parsing and failures it reports, and it never writes there, so the vault techniques that apply to a read-only consumer hold.

techniques.evidence: features/admin/getAdminData.ts:17 The read side is tolerant of hand-written, drifting markdown. Nothing here emits markdown, so the round-trip and minted-identity rules have nothing to check. Caveat: parsePassLog's strict regex quietly drops a pass heading that is not in the expected form.

features/admin/getAdminData.ts:126 Directory listings are flat (no recursion) and skip on error with reportLoaderFailure, which is the declared skip policy for a best-effort progress readout. The batch-NNN regex is copied twice in the same file rather than living in one shared helper, so drift is possible later.

features/admin/loops/getLoopState.ts:39 Each request reads the whole file fresh and holds no handle or lock, so a human editing the vault always wins. The app's only write is an append-only JSONL file in .data/, outside the vault.

features/admin/loops/loopState.ts:295 Loop staleness comes from the date written inside the graph-log pass heading, not from file mtime, so it survives a git checkout. Conflict copies are left out only by accident (the batch regex is anchored, the paths are fixed constants), and the code never says it excludes them.
features/admin/getAdminData.ts:13 Vault files are read straight from disk on every request; no relational or search mirror is built from them in this context.

pairs.registryProposal: The standard says nothing about a consumer that only reads a vault. Most techniques assume the app writes notes or keeps a mirror, so a read-only dashboard over a vault ends up with mostly unread or not-applicable verdicts. A short read-only-consumer profile (tolerant parse, fresh reads, in-band dates, declared skip policy) would make these pairs easier to judge.
